stories.title: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
stories.summary: Sign In Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Canada's top court has largely upheld a Quebec law banning public sector workers from wearing religious symbols, including the hijab and the cross. Quebec passed the law in 2019 under a unique fixture of Canada's constitution called the "notwithstanding clause" - a legal loophole that allows governments to override certain rights, like freedom of religion.

stories.title: Why is RBI bringing its gold back to India? The big shift decoded
